card.title: SHOGE DETACHMENT
card.flavorText: The Shoge Detachment was a unit of the 41st Division of the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII. The division was formed in 1939 and its first deployment was in the Shanxi province in China, where they were put on garrison duty. At the outbreak of the Pacific War in 1941 the division was based in Qingdao in eastern China, and the plan was to transfer it to Guadalcanal. However, after attempts to reinforce the Japanese garrison on the island failed, the decision was made to send it to New Guinea. As part of the 18th Army the 41st Division participated in the New Guinea campaign from 1943 to 45 where it fought against Australian and US forces. However, in 1943 the Shoge Detachment, named after their commander Ryoichi Shoge, was sent to fortify positions at Lae where it participated in the Salamaua–Lae Campaign under grueling circumstances. After being defeated at Lae, the Japanese forces decided to retreat to a new defensive line in the Huon Peninsula. Around 9,000 Japanese troops withdrew, and during the difficult retreat, the Japanese suffered heavy losses, both in manpower and equipment. Those that managed to reach their destination participated later in the Huon Peninsula Campaign, which was a series of battles fought in north-eastern Papua New Guinea in 1943 and 1944.
